newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China bars wife of dissident from entry.
newsitem.headline: China bars wife of dissident from entry.

text.p: The wife of Chinese dissident Wang Juntao, who was jailed for his role in the 1989 democracy movement in Beijing's Tiananmen Square, was barred from entering China, the Sunday Morning Post reported.

Hou Xiaotian, who was turned away from Beijing airport on Saturday, told the Hong Kong English language newspaper a Chinese customs official said she was rejected because of her involvement in "activities in opposition to the Chinese government".

Hou is known for her campaign which led to the release of Wang in 1994 on medical parole after he was sentenced to 13 years in prison for being involved in the 1989 pro-democracy movement, which was crushed by the government.
Flying to China from Seoul, South Korea, Hou had planned to stay a week in Beijing for a business workshop, but was put on the same plane and sent back to Seoul, the newspaper reported.
Hou then flew to Hong Kong late on Saturday, but said she was uncertain how long she will stay in the territory.
Hou's Saturday flight to China was her first attempt to return to the country since joining her husband in Boston in 1994, the newspaper said.
